conviction_note: Two findings point each way and none settles the print. The CEO said on 2026-09-08 that FY27 was 'on track', and by then the Q2 quarter (to 31 Aug) had closed. The bar was cut about 4% over 90 days and the stock went in 13.5% off its 31 Aug level at about 9.8x earnings. Against that: August was weak, Q1 left about 2 points of distributor inventory, diesel hit a record after the reaffirmation, and the industry fell 4.2% in calendar Q2. I lean slightly up (p_up 53) on a 5.5% absolute move, giving +0.33. The findings sum to +0.6; the two numbers agree in sign and differ in size because p_up carries the uncertainty that the +7.8-point put skew argues against.
bar: Q2 FY27 comparable EPS consensus $3.55-$3.62 and revenue $2.54-$2.57B. The sources disagree: Zacks has $3.62 / $2.57B (https://www.tradingview.com/news/zacks:1e6f80056094b:0-constellation-brands-pre-q2-earnings-is-it-poised-to-beat-estimates/), AlphaStreet $3.55 (https://news.alphastreet.com/constellation-brands-stz-q2-2027-preview-eps-est-3-55-reports-october-7/) and ScanX $3.56 / $2.54B (https://scanx.trade/stock-market-news/companies/constellation-brands-q2-earnings-analysts-eye-3-56-eps-2-54b-revenue/52747563). Two sources agree at about $3.55-3.56. Year-ago Q2 FY26 was comparable EPS $3.63 on revenue $2,481M (beer $2,345M, W&S $136M) (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000016918/000001691825000140/stzex991_83120258kearnings.htm). The company's own bar is the FY27 guide, affirmed 2026-06-30 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/16918/000001691826000028/stzex991_53120268kearnings.htm): comparable EPS $11.20-$11.90, beer net sales (1)% to +1%, beer operating margin 37-38%, OCF $2.4-2.5B, FCF $1.6-1.7B. Because the quarterly bar is disputed by about 2%, findings that depend on a quarterly beat are capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest was 8.5M shares at the 2026-09-15 settlement, up 4.2% from 8.2M, with 3.44 days to cover on about 2.5M shares of average daily volume (https://www.optionsanalysissuite.com/stocks/stz/short-interest). On 2026-07-15 it was 8.3M shares and 3.25 days to cover (https://equibles.com/stocks/stz/shortinterest). That is roughly 5% of float and not crowded, so there is no squeeze mechanism. Baseline: 25-delta skew +7.83 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 0.75, event-implied move 4.74%. The stock is 2.4% above its 52-week low and 30.7% below its high; 20-day run-up -4.56%, 5-day +2.39%. The sell side cut targets through September (Barclays 132->122, Deutsche Bank 150->136 on 09-11, Jefferies 147->135 on 09-14, JPMorgan 165->133 on 09-25, UBS 168->145, TD Cowen 174->150, Bernstein 197->180 on 09-28), and Zacks Rank is #4 with ESP -1.86%.

findings.finding: At the Barclays conference on 2026-09-08, eight days after Q2 (Jun-Aug) closed, CEO Nicholas Fink and CFO Garth Hankinson said FY27 guidance (comparable EPS $11.20-$11.90, beer net sales -1% to +1%) remains 'on track'. They also said Constellation was the World Cup's No. 1 beer share gainer at almost a full point, that August was 'pretty lackluster' on Circana data, and that the second half faces logistics and commodity inflation. The stock fell 5.1% to $120.43 the next day and has since drifted to about $113-115. Management knew the full Q2 quarter when it reaffirmed, so a Q2 collapse or an outright FY cut on 10-06 is less likely than the price action implies; a narrowing to the lower half is the plausible downside.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance is what this stock trades on. The FY27 guide on 2026-04-08 moved +8.53%. A January 2025 guide cut moved -17.09%, and a September 2025 guide cut (2025-09-02, bmo) moved -6.6%. A reaffirmed guide with a beat on 2026-06-30 moved -1.59%.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock fell on the August commentary and kept falling, another ~5% after the conference to near its 52-week low, while targets were cut. If the market fully credited a reaffirmation made with Q2 already closed, the stock would not have taken out its low and put skew would not be +7.8 points. Instead it is pricing a meaningful probability of a guide cut that management argued against a month ago.
findings.independence: Same event, second write-up: https://www.ad-hoc-news.de/boerse/news/corporate-news/constellation-brands-stock-falls-to-52-week-low-after-cautious-ceo/70080374 (2026-09-10), which shares the event and is not independent. A separate document, the 8-K of 2026-09-08 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/16918/000001691826000034/stzex991_90820268k.htm), carries only a note redemption and no guidance.

findings.finding: The year-ago shipment comparison is easy, and Q1 left an inventory build. Q2 FY26 beer shipments fell 8.7% against depletions of -2.7%, a roughly 6-point distributor destock, on beer net sales of $2,345M. In Q1 FY27 shipments rose 1.8% against depletions of -0.3%, about 2 points of rebuild. Consensus revenue of $2.54-2.57B less roughly $145M of W&S implies beer net sales of about +2% to +3.4%. With ~2% price, that needs shipments of about 0% to +1.5% yoy, which the 6-point destock in the comparison base makes reachable even with depletions slightly negative. The Q1 over-shipment is the offset.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 FY26 (2025-10-06) beat EPS on weak shipments and moved +1.03%. Q1 FY27 shipped ahead of depletions with a beat and moved -1.59%. Shipment-driven beats have bought little.
findings.why_not_priced: Previews quote consensus and depletion worries but none sets out the shipment-versus-depletion arithmetic against the destocked base. If it were priced, consensus revenue growth would sit visibly above the +3.6% Zacks figure, or below it if the Q1 build were the market's focus. The width of the consensus range ($2.54-2.57B) shows the bar is not settled.
findings.independence: Q1 FY27 release (a different document) for the +1.8% shipments against -0.3% depletions: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/16918/000001691826000028/stzex991_53120268kearnings.htm. Both are company primary documents.

findings.finding: US retail diesel set records after the 2026-09-08 reaffirmation: $5.85/gal on 09-04, $5.967 for the week of 09-07, and over $6 on 09-11. That is up about $2.26/gal since late February because of the US-Iran conflict and the Strait of Hormuz disruption. Management had already named logistics and diesel as a second-half headwind for FY27, so the risk is that the beer margin (37-38%) or EPS guide is trimmed or narrowed to the low end on 10-07.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Cost-driven guide changes have moved this stock hard: the April 2025 aluminum-tariff guide (+0.74%) and the September 2025 cut (-6.6%).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock is at its low and the September target cuts cite consumer and cost pressure. It is not fully priced because the company's last statement predates the move above $6. If the market had fully priced a margin cut, consensus FY EPS would sit below the guide's low end, but the guide range is still the reference in previews.
findings.independence: EIA record via Argus: https://www.argusmedia.com/es/news-and-insights/latest-market-news/2875742-eia-sharply-raises-2026-2027-diesel-price-forecast. The company's own naming of the logistics headwind is in finding 1's source. This is a macro proxy; transmission is confirmed by management only in direction.

findings.finding: The bar was cut into the print. Zacks consensus EPS fell 1.7% in a month and 4.1% in 90 days, from $3.70 to about $3.62, with other sources at $3.55-3.56. At least seven brokers cut targets between 09-11 and 09-28. The stock fell 13.5% from 31 Aug to $112.99 (09-30), at 9.8x the FY27 guide midpoint with a 3.65% yield. The last two prints off a depressed base, 2026-01-07 (+5.32%) and 2026-04-08 (+8.53%), rallied.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: From a lowered base: +5.32% (2026-01-07) and +8.53% (2026-04-08). From a less depressed base after a run-up: -1.59% (2026-06-30).
findings.why_not_priced: This sign runs against +7.8 points of put skew. The case that the option market is overpaying for downside: management confirmed the guide with Q2 closed, short interest is not crowded (3.4 days), and EPS and target cuts have already reset the bar. If this were priced, the stock would not be sitting 2.4% off its low with puts bid.

findings.finding: On 2026-08-06 Molson Coors estimated that the US beer industry fell 4.2% in calendar Q2 2026 (Apr-Jun), with its own US shipments down 7.3%. It blamed an energy and inflation shock from the Iran conflict, pump prices peaking in May, and consumers trading to convenience and dollar channels and smaller packs. Two of STZ's three Q2 months overlap that window. STZ depletions were -0.3% in Mar-May, roughly 4 points better than the industry, and management claimed a World Cup share gain.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Depletion misses drove the 2025 guide cuts (-17.09% and -6.6%). A -0.3% depletion print with a beat moved -1.59%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it is a public peer print two months old, and STZ's own August comment adds to it. Kept small. It matters only if STZ's Q2 depletions lost their relative outperformance, which the company's World Cup share claim argues against.
findings.independence: AB InBev Q2 2026 (2026-07-30) also reported lower US sales to retailers while claiming it beat the industry: https://www.beveragedaily.com/Article/2026/07/30/investment-and-innovation-boost-ab-inbev-sales/. This is an industry proxy, not an STZ number.

findings.finding: Routine refinancing. On 2026-09-08 STZ called all $600M of its 4.350% senior notes due 2027 for redemption on 2026-09-18. On 2026-09-18 it signed a $300M two-year delayed-draw term loan with M&T at SOFR+0.70-1.10% for general corporate purposes including debt repayment. The money refinances a near maturity at investment-grade spreads; it signals no distress and no ramp.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on financing.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and immaterial. Filed for completeness so a judge can see it was checked; the tight SOFR margin argues against any credit worry.

baseline_tension: My slight positive lean runs against +7.8 points of put skew and agrees with neither the -4.56% 20-day run-up nor the 52-week-low position. The case rests on management reaffirming with Q2 already closed and on a bar that has been cut, so p_up is held at 53 rather than higher.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar disputed: $3.55-3.56 vs $3.62): the shipment-comp finding, which depends on a quarterly beat, was capped from +0.3 to +0.2.
Rule 7 (sign against +7.8 put skew): the lowered-bar positioning finding went from +0.7 to +0.5, with the reason the skew may be wrong stated in why_not_priced; p_up held at 53.
Rule 1/3 (the stock fell 5% on the conference day despite the reaffirmation): the reaffirmation finding went from +1.0 to +0.8.
Rule 5 (macro proxy): diesel went from -0.8 to -0.6 and the Molson Coors industry proxy from -0.4 to -0.3; both kept, labelled as proxies.
Rule 4 (financing is a question): the refinancing was checked for what it buys (it repays 2027 notes) and stays at 0.
